obligation: Complaint record and investigation
trigger: A hospital report, researcher report, or other information alleging the device failed to meet its specifications, including a security failure
deadline: Record on receipt; review, evaluate, and investigate (no fixed day count in the regulation; internal target: complaint opened within 1 business day)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - every product security event is screened as a possible complaint

obligation: Medical device report (30-day)
trigger: Information that reasonably suggests the device may have caused or contributed to a death or serious injury, or malfunctioned in a way likely to do so if it recurred
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after the day the company becomes aware
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - VP QA/RA decides and documents

obligation: Medical device report (5-day)
trigger: An MDR reportable event needs remedial action to prevent an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the public health, or FDA asks in writing
deadline: No later than 5 work days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if remedial action is needed
clock_starts: An employee with management or supervisory responsibility over regulatory, scientific, or technical staff becomes aware that remedial action is needed (803.3)

obligation: MDR supplemental report
trigger: New information not known when the initial MDR was filed
deadline: Within 30 calendar days of receiving the information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an MDR was filed

obligation: Correction or removal report
trigger: The company initiates a correction or removal (for example a firmware fix or field action) to reduce a risk to health or remedy a violation that may present a risk to health
deadline: Within 10 working days of initiating the correction or removal (not required if already reported under part 803 or exempt under 806.1(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - unless all four enforcement-discretion conditions below are met
clock_starts: Initiation of the correction or removal

obligation: Record of a correction or removal not reported
trigger: A correction or removal that is not reportable (for example a routine update for a controlled risk) or handled under the enforcement-discretion policy
deadline: Keep the record with the justification, reviewed by a designated person; retain 2 years beyond the expected life of the device
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: customer communication (FDA enforcement-discretion condition)
citation: FDA guidance, Postmarket Management of Cybersecurity in Medical Devices (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Vulnerability assessed as an uncontrolled risk to safety and essential performance, with no known serious adverse events or deaths
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after learning of the vulnerability: describe the vulnerability and impact, state that work is underway, give compensating controls, and commit to communicating the fix
notify: Hospital customers and the user community; the ISAO (copy)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - guidance, not a regulation
clock_starts: The company learns of the vulnerability
owner: Director of Customer Support and Field Service (COO approves)

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: fix distributed (FDA enforcement-discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Same as above
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 60 days after learning of the vulnerability: fix, validate, and distribute; follow up with users beyond 60 days as needed
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - guidance; day-50 checkpoint in POL-03 4.6
clock_starts: The company learns of the vulnerability

obligation: ISAO participation and sharing (FDA enforcement-discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), sections VII.B and IX (nonbinding)
trigger: The company communicates with customers about a vulnerability
deadline: Share customer communications with the ISAO when customers are notified
notify: ISAO that shares medical device vulnerabilities
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - active member since 2024

obligation: Out-of-cycle update for critical vulnerabilities
trigger: Critical vulnerability that could cause uncontrolled risks in a cyber device or related system
deadline: Make updates and patches available out of cycle as soon as possible (no day count in the statute)
notify: Hospital customers via the update service or field service
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for VM-7, IP-4, and AI-001; VM-5 follows the postmarket guidance

obligation: Coordinated disclosure with the reporter
trigger: A researcher or other party reports a vulnerability
deadline: Acknowledge within 3 business days; agree a public disclosure date
notify: Reporter; optionally CISA for a coordinated public advisory
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company commitment

obligation: Business associate breach notice to hospitals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held in the CCC
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, or sooner under the BAA; include each affected individual's identity to the extent possible and other information the hospital needs
notify: Each affected hospital (covered entity) through the BAA contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CCC only
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the person committing it (164.410(a)(2))
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Security incident report under the BAA
trigger: Any security incident involving the CCC of which the company becomes aware
deadline: As set in each BAA (some as short as 5 business days); check the BAA terms register
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual timing varies by hospital

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented
notify: Hold hospital notices; document the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: State third-party agent notice (Florida worked example)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a); other states' agent provisions vary
trigger: Breach of a system the company maintains for a hospital that holds personal information of Florida individuals (medical information with a name counts)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determining the breach or having reason to believe it occurred; give the hospital what it needs for its notices
notify: Each affected Florida hospital (the covered entity under 501.171)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - shorter than the HIPAA 60-day limit, so it sets the clock for Florida hospitals; apply each other state's law for hospitals elsewhere
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Hospitals' own breach notices (information only)
trigger: A hospital determines a breach occurred
deadline: Hospital's deadlines; the company supplies information promptly
notify: Individuals, HHS, media, state regulators (by the hospital)
applies_at_this_tier: No - hospital duty; the company supports

obligation: State data breach notification (company-owned personal information, all states)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information the company holds for itself (for example employee records)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Only if company-owned personal information is affected; apply the law of each state where affected residents live (Florida rows below are the worked example)

obligation: State breach notice to individuals for company-owned personal information (Florida worked example)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(4); other states: each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Breach of employee or other personal information the company holds for itself (for example after plant ransomware reaches the office network)
deadline: Florida: no later than 30 days after determination (a 15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice to individuals); other states vary
applies_at_this_tier: Only if company-owned personal information is affected

obligation: State regulator notice for company-owned personal information (Florida worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida individuals
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no extension)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida individuals are affected

obligation: Consumer reporting agency notice (Florida worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 Florida individuals are notified

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion is involved (POL-03 4.9)

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; use the carrier hotline before hiring vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Lender and PE sponsor notice
citation: Credit agreement and sponsor reporting terms (contract)
trigger: Material cyber event or production stop
deadline: Per financing terms; CEO informs the sponsor's operating partner within 1 business day
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the proposed criteria would cover manufacturers of class II and III devices, so recheck when final
clock_starts: Proposed: reasonable belief of a covered incident

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no defense contracts

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
